[By Santhosh.B.. Advocate]
JUDGMENT

The charge sheet has been filed in this case by the Police SubI Inspector of Subramanyanagar police station against the accused no.1 to 3 for the alleged offences punishable under Sections 341, 498A,
323, 504 and 506 r/w Sec. 34 of IPC.
2.

In briefly the case of the prosecution is as follows:-
It is the case of the prosecution that the accused no.1 married C.W.1- Ms.Bhavya on 02.12.2018 and out of wedlock, the accused No.1 and C.W.1 were blessed with a male baby, further while C.W.1 was pregnant, the accused No.1 to 3 with an intention to commit an offence and in furtherance of their common intention forced C.W.1 to go to work and subjected C.W.1 to mental cruelty by abusing her in filthy language and drove her out of the matrimonial house, further while the accused No.1 and C.W.1 were made to live together in a separate house, the accused No.1 used to consume alcohol and would assault the child and extended physical and mental cruelty towards C.W.1.

Further on 05.12.2022 at house No.30370, 10th main,
GayathriNagar, the accused no.1 had consumed alcohol and went home and without any provocation assaulted and kicked C.W.1 and caused hurt and criminally intimidated to C.W1 by showing her a knife.
Therefore the C.C.2699/2023 C.W.1 lodged the complaint against accused no.1 to 3 before the Subramanyanagar Police seeking necessary action against them in accordance with law.
3. On the basis of the said complaint given by C.W.1, the complainant police have registered the case under Crime No.186/2022 and sent FIR to this Court and to their concerned higher authorities.

Thereafter, the complainant police have visited the spot and conducted the spot mahazar in the presence of the panch witnesses, herein after recorded the statements of witnesses who availed in the station subsequently who availed where the said mahazars have been drawn, after completion of the investigation the IO has arived at a conclusion that there are sufficient materials as to prosecute the accused no.1 to 3 , for which charge sheet has been filed for the above said offences.

4. After filing of the charge sheet, this Court registered the case is as numbered above, before that the accused no.1 to 3 was enlarged on bail, meanwhile copies of the charge sheet and other prosecution papers were duly supplied as required under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.

After hearing both sides, this court found that there were sufficient reasons so as to frame charge against the accused no.1 to 3 , therefore charge was framed and read over and explained to the accused no.1 to 3 in the language known to them, after understanding the same they denied the same and claimed to be tried, accordingly, proceeded with trial.
5. In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined one witness who is said to be victim as P.W.1 and got marked two documents at Ex.P-1 and 2.

As there are no any incriminating materials Subramanyanagar Police Station vs Sunil Kumar on 29 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88777338/
2 forth coming against the accused no.1 to 3 , as to which summoning of remaining C.C.2699/2023 witnesses would no purpose to serve and therefore CW-2 to 8 ordered to be given up by rejecting the submission made by the learned PP.

sentences.text: Consequently, recording of statement of accused no.1 to 3 as required under section 313 of Cr.P.C also dispensed with.

6. Heard both side arguments, in compliance of section 437-A of Cr.P.C., bail bond were obtained from the accused no.1 to 3 .
7.

In view of above said facts and circumstances the following points that would arise for my consideration are as follows:-
POINTS FOR CONSIDERATION 1.

Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused no.1 married C.W.1-Ms.Bhavya on 02.12.2018 and out of wedlock, the accused No.1 and C.W.1 were blessed with a male baby, further while C.W.1 was pregnant, the accused No.1 to 3 with an intention to commit an offence and in furtherance of their common intention forced C.W.1 to go to work and subjected C.W.1 to mental cruelty by abusing her in filthy language and drove her out of the matrimonial house, further while the accused No.1 and C.W.1 were made to live together in a separate house, the accused No.1 used to consume alcohol and would assault the child and extended physical and mental cruelty towards C.W.1 and thereby the accused no.1 to 3 have committed an offence punishable under section 498A r/w Sec.34 of IPC?

2. Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that while the C.W.1 was residing at the matrimonial house the accused no.1 to 3 with an intention to commit an offence and in furtherance of that intention, abused C.W.1 in filthy language knowingly that it would give provocation to C.W.1 to breach C.C.2699/2023 public peace and thereby the accused no.1 to 3 committed the offence of "intentional insult"
punishable U/s 504 r/w Sec.34 of IPC?

3. Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that on on 05.12.2022 at house No.30370, 10th main, GayathriNagar, the accused no.1 had consumed alcohol and went home and without any provocation assaulted and kicked C.W.1 and caused hurt and thereby the accused no.1 committed the offence of "voluntrily causing hurt " punishable U/s 323of IPC?

4. Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused no.1 to 3 criminally intimidated to the life of C.W1 and thereby the accused no.1 to 3 has committed an offence of "criminal intimidation"

3 punishable U/s 506 r/w Sec. 34 of IPC?
5.

8. My answers to the above points are as under:
Point Nos.1 to 4 In the 'Negative' Point No.5 As per the final order, for the following:-
REASONS 9. Point No.1 to 4 : These points are taken up together for common discussion in order to avoid the repetation of facts.
10. In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined the complainant/C.W.1 as P.W.1 and got marked two documents on her behalf as Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2.

As far as appreciation of oral and documentary evidence is concerned P.W.1 is the complainant by name Bhavya, she deposed in her evidence that accused no.1 is her husband, accused no.2 and are the mother and maternal uncle of accused no.1.
C.C.2699/2023
and her marriage with the accused no.1 was an arranged marriage, her marriage was solemnized witha accused no.1 on 02/12/2018, Bengaluru.
After marriage she resided along with the accused no.1 and 2, she is blessed with one son.

She further deposed that the accused have not physically and mentally harassed her, did not abuse her, did not assault her and the accused no.1 did not consume alcohol and did not threaten her with dire consequences.
She has not been lodged complaint against the accused no.1 to 3 before police station.
She identified her signature in the complaint which is marked as Ex.p.1 and her signature is marked as Ex.P.1(a).
In the year 2022 when she visited Subramanyanagar P.S, at the request of police she put her signature on Ex.P.1.
She further deposed that she does not know the contents of Ex.P.1.
Witness identified her signature in the spot mahazar which is marked as Ex.P2 and her signature is marked as Ex.P.2(a).
She further deposed that at that event there were no people present in the said spot.
She has not shown any spot to the police.
Police have not drawn any mahazar in her presence.

She does not know the contents of Ex.P 1 and 2 and she has not given any documents to the police during the course of investigation, as to which when learned Assistant Public Prosecutor treated this witness as hostile and with the permission of the court, cross-examined her even in that process also learned A.P.P. failed to elicit anything from her mouth.

11. As the first informant/complainant P.W.1 being the material witness in this case has not supported the case of the prosecution and as she turned hostile by giving a complete go-bye statement, due to which other prosecution witness were given up, as it would serve no purpose to summon the other witnesses, during the course of C.C.2699/2023 prosecution evidence two documents got marked as Ex.P1 and P.2.

So far as Ex.P1 is the complaint and Ex.P.2 is the spot mahazar, but the prosecution witness did not support the contents which are mentioned in the same, therefore whatever the suspicious circumstances pleaded while framing of charge remained as same.

On considering these facts herein no incriminating materials forthcoming against the accused Subramanyanagar Police Station vs Sunil Kumar on 29 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88777338/

sentences.text: 4 no.1 to 3 persons and the prosecution has not established the ingredients of the alleged offences against the accused no.1 to 3 no.1 however herein no positive evidence to prove the guilt of the accused no.1 to 3 no.1 , for which this Court is of the considered opinion that prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused no.1 to 3 no.1 beyond all reasonable doubt.

Hence, benefit of doubt goes to the accused no.1 to 3 no.1, for which I answer point Nos.1 to 4 in the 'Negative'.
12. Point No.5:

In view of my findings on point Nos.1 to 5 and reasons assigned therein, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Acting under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C., the accused no.1 to 3 are not found guilty and they are hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Secs.498A,
504, 323 and 506 of IPC .
The bail bond executed by the accused no.1 to 3 stands cancelled.

In compliance of section 437-A of Cr.P.C. the bail bond executed by the accused no.1 to 3 is C.C.2699/2023 ordered to be continued in force for six months or till issuance of notice in respect of any appeal [if preferred] against the present Judgment before the Appellate Court.
